subject: Clarify: what stays vs what gets flushed by default (requests, prompts, outputs)
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brightbank.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: what you keep by default (prompts vs answers)

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for taking this early call with our procurement team last week. Procurement needs plain-language answers so they can draft the SOW. A few specific items we need clarified for BrightBank's security and compliance reviewers:

1) By default, what does Redwood store when our app calls the hosted API? Specifically: the user prompt, intermediate streaming fragments, final model answer, and any generated artifacts (attachments).
2) How long is each of those elements retained by default? We need both the standard host (no add-ons) and any known variation for the Dedicated/Private deployments.
3) Where does the data physically reside by default (region) and can we force EU-only residency for this account?
4) If we request erasure, what's the timeline and what proof do you provide that data was removed (proof-of-deletion artifact)?

I've attached a short sample_prompts.txt and a draft procurement checklist. We're trying to avoid vague language — the security folks want explicit fields and timelines.

Would appreciate a one-email summary we can hand to legal and procurement.

Best,
Elena Ramos
Lead, Procurement & Vendor Risk
BrightBank

Attachment: sample_prompts.txt (3 lines sample)

Subject: Re: Questions: what you keep by default (prompts vs answers)

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear checklist. Below is a concise, plain-language summary you can pass to procurement/legal. I'll keep it high level and call out options for Dedicated/Private.

SUMMARY (plain language)
- "User input / prompt": By default we store the request payload (the raw user input and metadata) for 30 days to support debugging, abuse detection, and customer support. Customers can opt-out at call time (store=false) for new requests; opt-out does not retroactively remove previously stored records.

- "Streaming fragments / interim tokens": Ephemeral by default. Stream fragments are buffered for up to 7 days for reconnection/debugging only and are not consolidated into the customer's searchable logs. They are separated from final outputs and cleared sooner.

- "Final model answer / generated output": Kept by default for 90 days. This retention exists so we can investigate quality/regressions and provide customers with request history. If a customer chooses the "no-store" flag on the request or configures account-level data governance (Dedicated/Private), final outputs can be prevented from persisting.

- "Attachments / uploaded files": Stored with the same retention as the request that referenced them (default 30 days) unless you ask for a different retention in your contract. For Dedicated or Private deployments we can mirror your SOW retention (contractual).

- "KV cache and runtime caches": Not persisted to long-term storage by default. KV cache is runtime-only and flushed on pod restart; not available as a stored artifact for erasure requests.

- "Operational logs & audit records (billing/trace)": Separate from request/response artifacts. We retain operational audit logs for up to 365 days for billing, security, and compliance reasons; we can scope export/erasure requests but some platform-level logs are retained for forensic/audit compliance as allowed by the SOW.

DATA RESIDENCY
- Hosted API: defaults to the region of the customer's tenancy; for new accounts you can select "us" or "eu" regions. BrightBank can be configured to EU-only residency for hosted if requested during onboarding (we'll lock region and include residency clause in SOW).
- Dedicated / Private: you control the VPC/region and can keep all data on-prem or in an EU region.

ERASURE / PROOF OF DELETION
- Erasure process: 1) Customer requests deletion via Console or support ticket. 2) We validate scope and schedule deletion. 3) Deletion job runs (background) and removes records from primary and replica stores; tombstones/indices are compacted per our purge window.
- Timeline: For standard hosted accounts, typical completion is 3–10 business days depending on volume and replication lag.
- Proof: We provide a signed deletion report (CSV of deleted record ids with timestamps) plus a system-generated audit ticket id. For legal/audit we can produce a certificate of deletion and associated archive logs showing the job ran.

OPTIONS / CONTRACT LANGUAGE YOU CAN COPY
- "Customer data (user prompts and outputs) will be retained by Redwood Inference for a period of 30 days for request payloads and 90 days for generated outputs, unless a 'no-store' flag is used or a different retention is agreed in writing. Operational audit logs will be retained for up to 365 days. Region-specific residency will be applied per account onboarding and can be restricted to EU regions on request"

I'll loop Marissa and Karthik for any technical/legal nuances I missed. If you'd like, we can convert this to a single-page SOW paragraph.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Elena & Soojin — adding a couple of concrete bullets we include in SOWs and legal reviews:

- Proof-of-deletion: our standard deliverable is a deletion-report CSV (deleted_record_id, type, deletion_timestamp, job_id) signed by our compliance team. For high-assurance customers we can also provide MD5 hashes of deleted objects (where applicable) and an internal audit trail that shows when compaction jobs ran.

- No-store flag: technically implemented as a header (x-redwood-store=false). This prevents writes to persistent stores for both request payload and final output. Note: some derived telemetry (aggregate counters, billing metrics) remains for billing and SLA enforcement; those aggregates are non-reidentifiable in standard reporting.

- Dedicated / Private: we typically mirror your SOW retention exactly. If you require longer retention for a pilot (e.g., 12 months), we will set a contract override and include a data retention schedule in Annex A of the SOW.

I've attached a quick retention_matrix_v1.csv that maps artifact -> default retention -> opt-out capability. Happy to formalize this into one contract paragraph if helpful.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

2) On proof-of-deletion: can you confirm the deletion-report CSV will include the original customer record ids (not Redwood internal ids)? Legal wants traceability back to our records.

If you can confirm those two items I'll route this to Legal and Procurement today.
